description: Search or list vendor-published advisories, newest first. A query of 3 or more characters is matched case-insensitively as a substring of each advisory's title, description, vendor name, IDs and affected_products (search_match substring). A query of 1 or 2 characters matches whole words only (search_match word). Filter by vendor (slug), severity band and whether the advisory names any CVE ID. Advisories their vendor withdrew are left out. Returns advisories, each with vendor, vendor_advisory_id, title, severity, cvss_v3_score, cve_ids, summary and affected_products where present, and total, total_capped, limit, offset, search_applied and search_match. A search counts at most 1,000 matches: past that, total is 1000 and total_capped is true, which means 1,000 or more (the note writes 1,000+), never exactly 1,000. Each advisory also carries rejected_cve_ids: the CVE IDs it names whose CVE record was rejected (withdrawn) by its numbering authority, which are not active vulnerabilities. The query is sent in a request header, never in the URL. coverage repeats those beside returned, and gives vendor_windows, each vendor's window in what EchelonGraph holds: vendor, advisories, earliest_vendor_published_at, latest_vendor_published_at, held_since (where that window begins), history_backfill (in_progress or not_started: older advisories not all held yet), history_scope and feed_held_since. An advisory published before its vendor's held_since may not be held, so no advisory from a vendor is not a finding that it published none. Past 30,000 characters of JSON, the first text block holds data cut to fit, and the note says what the cut leaves out and where to read it (TEXT CUT); so is structured data (DATA CUT), unless full: true. Cut, each row keeps vendor, vendor_advisory_id, title, severity and cve_ids at least, its strings and lists shortened, or rows are left out and the note gives the offset to call next.

full.description: true: data in the structured result is the answer whole, however long. Without it, a structured result past 30,000 characters of JSON has its data cut (DATA CUT): in an order the note states, the entries of its longest lists keep only some of their fields, and then the lists only some of their entries; data_truncated is true, and truncated gives each list cut with its total, the number returned and whether its entries are thinned. Whole data is for a program; a client that sizes structured results, as Claude Code does against MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS, can refuse an answer past its cap.

has_cve.description: true: only advisories naming a CVE; false: only those naming none

query.description: free text, at most 100 bytes: a product, an advisory ID, a CVE ID or a keyword, e.g. 'exchange server'; 1 or 2 characters match whole words only

vendor.description: a vendor slug, e.g. microsoft, redhat, github

name: search_vendor_advisories

search_match.description: word: a query of 1 or 2 characters, matched as a whole word only; substring: a longer query; null without a query.

total.description: The API's total; when total_capped is true, a lower bound, not the count.

total_capped.description: true: total is the API's cap on a search's count, so 1,000 or more match.

items.description: A vendor's window in what EchelonGraph holds: vendor, advisories (how many EchelonGraph holds from that vendor), earliest_vendor_published_at and latest_vendor_published_at (the earliest and latest vendor_published_at among them, null when none is held), held_since (the start of the window EchelonGraph has read that vendor's advisories from, before which an advisory may not be held; null when none is held or the API does not say; for a vendor with no history read it is when its feed was first read from, and can be years after earliest_vendor_published_at, since an older advisory is held when the vendor revised it later, not the ones published beside it; where history_scope is a part of the vendor's advisories, it is where that part is held from, and the rest is held from feed_held_since), feed_held_since (the start of the window the vendor's own feed has read every one of its advisories from, which is held_since as it would be without any history read; an advisory outside history_scope published before it may not be held; null when none is held or the API does not say), history_backfill: complete (the vendor's published history has been read back as far as its source goes), complete_reviewed_only (the vendor's reviewed advisories have been read back as far as its source goes and its unreviewed ones have not: GitHub's, history_scope reviewed), in_progress or not_started (it is still being read, so the vendor's older advisories are not all held yet), or not_supported (EchelonGraph has no history read for that vendor, so what it holds is what the vendor's feed has carried), history_scope (what the vendor's history read covers: all, or reviewed for GitHub, whose read covers its reviewed advisories and not its unreviewed ones, which are held only from feed_held_since; a value the API adds later as it sends it; null for a vendor with no history read, or when the API does not say), and last_success_at (the vendor's last successful poll), collection_state (whether the vendor is being collected now, by EchelonGraph's feed-state rule: ok; partial, its polls succeed but held_back of the documents it lists could not be used, the oldest since held_back_since, and those advisories, or those revisions, may not be held while the rest of its feed is; failing, it is not being collected, and what it published after failing_since, its last successful poll, may not be held, whatever the window says; disabled, this deployment runs no collector for it (its held advisories are still served), so its window ends at last_success_at; a value the API adds later as it sends it, never read as ok), failing_since, held_back and held_back_since (each null when the API does not say).

advisories.description: How many advisories EchelonGraph holds from this vendor, withdrawn ones not counted.

collection_state.description: Whether this vendor is being collected now, by EchelonGraph's feed-state rule: ok, partial, failing or disabled. ok: it is being collected. partial: its polls succeed, but held_back of the documents it lists could not be used, the oldest since held_back_since; those advisories, or those revisions, may not be held, and the rest of its feed is. failing: it is not being collected, and an advisory it published after failing_since, its last successful poll, may not be held, whatever the window says. disabled: this deployment runs no collector for it (its held advisories are still served), so its window ends at last_success_at, and an advisory it published after that may not be held. A value the API adds later is relayed as sent and is not read as ok. null when the API does not say.

earliest_vendor_published_at.description: The earliest vendor_published_at among them; null when none is held. Not where the window begins: see held_since.

failing_since.description: While collection_state is failing, this vendor's last successful poll: an advisory it published after it may not be held, whatever the window says. null when it is not failing, when no successful poll is on record, or when the API does not say.

feed_held_since.description: The start of the window this vendor's own feed has read every one of its advisories from: held_since as it would be without any history read, and equal to it for a vendor with no history read. Where history_scope is a part of the vendor's advisories (reviewed: GitHub's history read covers its reviewed advisories only), an advisory outside it published before feed_held_since may not be held, however early held_since is. null when none is held or the API does not say.

held_back.description: How many of the documents this vendor lists EchelonGraph could not use (collection_state partial): those advisories, or those revisions, may not be held. 0 when none is held back; null when the API does not say.

held_back_since.description: When the oldest held-back document first failed; null when none is held back or the API does not say.

held_since.description: The start of the window EchelonGraph has read this vendor's advisories from; null when none is held or the API does not say. An advisory this vendor published before it may not be held, even when earliest_vendor_published_at is older. Where history_scope is a part of the vendor's advisories (reviewed), it is where that part is held from; the rest is held from feed_held_since.

history_backfill.description: history_backfill: complete (the vendor's published history has been read back as far as its source goes), complete_reviewed_only (the vendor's reviewed advisories have been read back as far as its source goes and its unreviewed ones have not: GitHub's, history_scope reviewed), in_progress or not_started (it is still being read, so the vendor's older advisories are not all held yet), or not_supported (EchelonGraph has no history read for that vendor, so what it holds is what the vendor's feed has carried).

history_scope.description: What this vendor's history read covers: all (every advisory its archive publishes) or reviewed (GitHub: its reviewed advisories, not its unreviewed ones, which are held only from feed_held_since); a value the API adds later as it sends it. null for a vendor with no history read, or when the API does not say.

last_success_at.description: This vendor's last successful poll; null when none is on record or the API does not say. While collection_state is disabled, the window ends here.

latest_vendor_published_at.description: The latest vendor_published_at among them; null when none is held.

vendor_windows.description: Each vendor's window in what EchelonGraph holds, only that vendor's when vendor is given; null when the windows could not be read. An advisory a vendor published before its held_since may not be held, even when its earliest_vendor_published_at is older, and one outside its history_scope (GitHub's unreviewed advisories) published before its feed_held_since may not be held either, nor one it published after its last successful poll while its collection_state is failing or disabled, nor one of the documents it holds back (partial), so no advisory from a vendor is not a finding that it published none.

coverage.description: What the answer covers; null where the answer says nothing about it.

advisory_id.description: EchelonGraph's internal ID for this advisory, a UUID. It is not the vendor's advisory ID (vendor_advisory_id), and an advisory's detail is not looked up by it: the detail is keyed on vendor and vendor_advisory_id.

cvss_v3_vector.description: The CVSS v3 vector of cvss_v3_score where the vendor's source carries one (Microsoft's); null otherwise. On by-cve rows and the detail.

our_first_seen_at.description: When EchelonGraph first recorded the advisory; not the vendor's date.

rejected_cve_ids.description: The CVE IDs this advisory names whose CVE record was rejected (withdrawn) by its numbering authority: each is a rejected record, not an active vulnerability, whatever the advisory's text says. The vendor's withdrawn is separate and unchanged by it. [] when none is; null when that could not be checked.

remediation_kinds.description: The kinds of remediation the advisory lists (for the CVE asked about, on a by-cve row), each the vendor's own category (vendor_fix, workaround, mitigation, no_fix_planned, none_available or other), or may be no_fix_planned where a Cisco advisory's summary says no fix will be released. [] with remediation_state not_parsed is not a finding that it lists none.

remediation_state.description: parsed; none_in_source (EchelonGraph read the vendor's remediation, and it lists none for this CVE, which is not a finding that no fix exists); not_parsed (EchelonGraph does not read this vendor's remediation, or has not yet read this advisory: not a finding of none); withdrawn (the vendor rescinded the advisory).

vendor.description: The vendor's slug. Each vendor's advisory data stays under its own licence, and EchelonGraph's terms add no restriction to it: redhat, Red Hat's security advisories, © Red Hat, Inc., licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/; source https://access.redhat.com/security/data); github, the GitHub Advisory Database, licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/; source https://github.com/github/advisory-database); microsoft, Microsoft's own terms (its advisory pages are not copied: the facts and EchelonGraph's title are served, with a link to Microsoft's advisory where it names a CVE ID); every other vendor, that vendor's own terms.

vendor_advisory_id.description: The vendor's own ID for the advisory (e.g. RHSA-2024:1234, GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx, or the CVE ID for Microsoft and Palo Alto Networks). With vendor, it is the key an advisory's detail is looked up by, as its advisory_id argument.

vendor_published_at.description: The date the vendor gives for the advisory.

vendor_text_withheld.description: true: the vendor's advisory page is not copied (Microsoft's): title is EchelonGraph's (Microsoft security update for its first CVE where it lists a vendor fix, Microsoft advisory otherwise, by its own ID when it names no CVE), and the advisory's description, summary, remediation, withdrawn_reason and each remediation's text are empty (instead, a detail's cve_records lists the first cve_records_cap CVEs it names, each with the CVE record's description or null, as cve_records says when); severity, cvss_v3_score, cvss_v3_vector, cve_ids, affected_products, the dates and the links are the vendor's facts, and, where the advisory names a CVE ID, references lead with the vendor's own advisory page.

withdrawn.description: true: the vendor withdrew (rescinded) this advisory, so it is a withdrawn advisory, not a current one.

search_applied.description: Whether a free-text search filtered this answer.

search_match.description: How the query was matched: word (a query of 1 or 2 characters, whole words only) or substring; null without a query. A query of 3 or more characters is matched case-insensitively as a substring of each advisory's title, description, vendor name, vendor_advisory_id, affected_products and cve_ids (search_match substring). A query of 1 or 2 characters matches whole words only (search_match word): it must equal, ignoring case, a whole word (a run of letters and digits) of one of those, so xz finds xz-utils but not xzibit, and a 1- or 2-character query with any other character, such as c#, matches nothing.

total.description: The matches; when total_capped is true, a lower bound: 1,000 or more.

total_capped.description: true: the search stopped counting at total, so total is a lower bound (1,000+), not the count. A search counts at most 1,000 matches: past that, total is 1000 and total_capped is true, which means 1,000 or more (the note writes 1,000+), never exactly 1,000; paging past it still works. Without a query, total is the exact count and total_capped is false.

data_truncated.description: false: data is the answer whole. true: the structured result would pass 30,000 characters of JSON with data whole, so data is cut (DATA CUT): the entries of some of its lists keep only some of their fields, or the lists only some of their entries, truncated gives each, and no string is shortened. The same call with full: true returns data whole.

freshness.description: The producing radar's last completed check (last_run_at), where the API serves one.

measured_at.description: When the underlying observation was made, as the API states it; null when the answer does not say or holds no observation.

state.description: measured: a measurement of what was asked; an exposure count is measured only with measured_at and method. not_assessed: the answer holds no dated measurement of what was asked, so no count in it is presented as one; it can still relay a count, as what the source holds on record, undated, and its notes (and exposure_state, where the result carries it) say what each count is.

truncated.description: Present when data_truncated is true: each list of data that was cut, by its path in data (a dot between the names of an object and a list inside it), with total, its entries in the answer, returned, the entries data holds, and thinned, true when each of them keeps only some of its fields.

search_match.description: word: a query of 1 or 2 characters, matched as a whole word only; substring: a longer query; null without a query.

total.description: The API's total; when total_capped is true, a lower bound, not the count.

total_capped.description: true: total is the API's cap on a search's count, so 1,000 or more match.

items.description: A vendor's window in what EchelonGraph holds: vendor, advisories (how many EchelonGraph holds from that vendor), earliest_vendor_published_at and latest_vendor_published_at (the earliest and latest vendor_published_at among them, null when none is held), held_since (the start of the window EchelonGraph has read that vendor's advisories from, before which an advisory may not be held; null when none is held or the API does not say; for a vendor with no history read it is when its feed was first read from, and can be years after earliest_vendor_published_at, since an older advisory is held when the vendor revised it later, not the ones published beside it; where history_scope is a part of the vendor's advisories, it is where that part is held from, and the rest is held from feed_held_since), feed_held_since (the start of the window the vendor's own feed has read every one of its advisories from, which is held_since as it would be without any history read; an advisory outside history_scope published before it may not be held; null when none is held or the API does not say), history_backfill: complete (the vendor's published history has been read back as far as its source goes), complete_reviewed_only (the vendor's reviewed advisories have been read back as far as its source goes and its unreviewed ones have not: GitHub's, history_scope reviewed), in_progress or not_started (it is still being read, so the vendor's older advisories are not all held yet), or not_supported (EchelonGraph has no history read for that vendor, so what it holds is what the vendor's feed has carried), history_scope (what the vendor's history read covers: all, or reviewed for GitHub, whose read covers its reviewed advisories and not its unreviewed ones, which are held only from feed_held_since; a value the API adds later as it sends it; null for a vendor with no history read, or when the API does not say), and last_success_at (the vendor's last successful poll), collection_state (whether the vendor is being collected now, by EchelonGraph's feed-state rule: ok; partial, its polls succeed but held_back of the documents it lists could not be used, the oldest since held_back_since, and those advisories, or those revisions, may not be held while the rest of its feed is; failing, it is not being collected, and what it published after failing_since, its last successful poll, may not be held, whatever the window says; disabled, this deployment runs no collector for it (its held advisories are still served), so its window ends at last_success_at; a value the API adds later as it sends it, never read as ok), failing_since, held_back and held_back_since (each null when the API does not say).

advisories.description: How many advisories EchelonGraph holds from this vendor, withdrawn ones not counted.

collection_state.description: Whether this vendor is being collected now, by EchelonGraph's feed-state rule: ok, partial, failing or disabled. ok: it is being collected. partial: its polls succeed, but held_back of the documents it lists could not be used, the oldest since held_back_since; those advisories, or those revisions, may not be held, and the rest of its feed is. failing: it is not being collected, and an advisory it published after failing_since, its last successful poll, may not be held, whatever the window says. disabled: this deployment runs no collector for it (its held advisories are still served), so its window ends at last_success_at, and an advisory it published after that may not be held. A value the API adds later is relayed as sent and is not read as ok. null when the API does not say.

earliest_vendor_published_at.description: The earliest vendor_published_at among them; null when none is held. Not where the window begins: see held_since.

failing_since.description: While collection_state is failing, this vendor's last successful poll: an advisory it published after it may not be held, whatever the window says. null when it is not failing, when no successful poll is on record, or when the API does not say.

feed_held_since.description: The start of the window this vendor's own feed has read every one of its advisories from: held_since as it would be without any history read, and equal to it for a vendor with no history read. Where history_scope is a part of the vendor's advisories (reviewed: GitHub's history read covers its reviewed advisories only), an advisory outside it published before feed_held_since may not be held, however early held_since is. null when none is held or the API does not say.

held_back.description: How many of the documents this vendor lists EchelonGraph could not use (collection_state partial): those advisories, or those revisions, may not be held. 0 when none is held back; null when the API does not say.

held_back_since.description: When the oldest held-back document first failed; null when none is held back or the API does not say.

held_since.description: The start of the window EchelonGraph has read this vendor's advisories from; null when none is held or the API does not say. An advisory this vendor published before it may not be held, even when earliest_vendor_published_at is older. Where history_scope is a part of the vendor's advisories (reviewed), it is where that part is held from; the rest is held from feed_held_since.

history_backfill.description: history_backfill: complete (the vendor's published history has been read back as far as its source goes), complete_reviewed_only (the vendor's reviewed advisories have been read back as far as its source goes and its unreviewed ones have not: GitHub's, history_scope reviewed), in_progress or not_started (it is still being read, so the vendor's older advisories are not all held yet), or not_supported (EchelonGraph has no history read for that vendor, so what it holds is what the vendor's feed has carried).

history_scope.description: What this vendor's history read covers: all (every advisory its archive publishes) or reviewed (GitHub: its reviewed advisories, not its unreviewed ones, which are held only from feed_held_since); a value the API adds later as it sends it. null for a vendor with no history read, or when the API does not say.

last_success_at.description: This vendor's last successful poll; null when none is on record or the API does not say. While collection_state is disabled, the window ends here.

latest_vendor_published_at.description: The latest vendor_published_at among them; null when none is held.

vendor_windows.description: Each vendor's window in what EchelonGraph holds, only that vendor's when vendor is given; null when the windows could not be read. An advisory a vendor published before its held_since may not be held, even when its earliest_vendor_published_at is older, and one outside its history_scope (GitHub's unreviewed advisories) published before its feed_held_since may not be held either, nor one it published after its last successful poll while its collection_state is failing or disabled, nor one of the documents it holds back (partial), so no advisory from a vendor is not a finding that it published none.

kind.description: What failed: the request (network, timeout), the answer (http, not_json, not_object, unexpected_shape), the input, or this server.

message.description: The cause: the API's own message, or what went wrong.

path.description: The API path requested, when a request was made.

status.description: The HTTP status, when the API answered one; 503 with kind internal and path null where this server was too busy to make the call.

state.description: failed: the lookup did not complete. invalid_input: the input was refused, so nothing was looked up. Neither is a finding.
